defaults.permitted_development: Across West Sussex, a temporary building is not exempt simply because it will be removed later. The planning answer usually turns on how fixed it is, how long it remains, what it is used for and whether any specific temporary-use right actually applies.

rules.height_rules: There is no standard height allowance for temporary buildings. The taller and more engineered the structure looks, the harder it is to present it as a minor temporary feature rather than operational development needing permission.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. Footprint, duration, services, foundations and the intensity of use matter far more than one single measurement.
rules.boundary_rules: Across West Sussex, access, traffic, noise, overlooking, servicing and visibility at the site edge are often what turn a supposedly temporary structure into a proposal that needs fuller planning scrutiny.
rules.roof_rules: A fixed or heavily engineered roof can quickly make a temporary structure look permanent. Wind loading, rainwater handling and visual bulk all matter.
rules.materials_rules: Use reversible, low-glare materials and temporary-looking details. Heavy cladding, permanent foundations and hard-wired services tend to undermine the temporary case.

rules.permitted_development: The word temporary does not settle the planning position. What matters is how long the structure remains, how fixed it is and what activity it supports. rules.height_rules: Height for a temporary building is judged through bulk, visibility and whether the structure still reads as genuinely short-term rather than semi-permanent. rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. Footprint, duration, services, foundations and the overall intensity of use matter much more than one single measurement.
rules.boundary_rules: The harder boundary questions are usually operational: how people arrive, where vehicles stop, what neighbours hear and how visible the structure becomes at the plot edge. In Adur, access, parking, overlooking and loss of openness are often the practical boundary issues.
rules.roof_rules: A fixed or fully engineered roof can push a proposal toward being treated as a building rather than a lightweight temporary structure. Wind resistance, rainwater disposal and visual bulk all matter.
rules.materials_rules: Use reversible, low-glare materials and details that support the temporary case. Heavy cladding, permanent foundations and utility connections make the structure harder to describe as temporary. On exposed or visitor-facing sites, anchoring, appearance and clutter can become bigger issues than the word temporary suggests.

restrictions.conservation_area: A temporary structure in a conservation area still has to look genuinely temporary, stay visually quiet and avoid cluttering the historic setting.
restrictions.listed_building: Where a temporary structure affects a listed building or its setting, the heritage route usually needs to be checked alongside the ordinary planning position.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can still remove fallback rights for temporary structures in selected locations, so the exact site designation should be checked before relying on a simpler route.
